title: Concept Vector Homogeneity Across Model Layers: Are Safety Concepts Polysemantic

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: polysemantic safety vectors cause collateral suppression of unrelated content. Understanding and resolving this is a prerequisite for precise steering. The SAE decomposition approach is well-motivated by recent interpretability work.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Using Sparse Autoencoders to decompose concept vectors requires understanding of SAE training and interpretation, which is an active research area. Pre-trained SAEs exist for some models but applying them to concept vectors requires non-trivial technical expertise beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two-part experiment: polysemanticity test (measure cross-concept accuracy) and SAE decomposition. The polysemanticity test alone is well-scoped; adding SAE decomposition extends significantly. Could be narrowed to just the cross-concept accuracy measurement.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
